exact_identity.vote-desc: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

substantive_actions.primary_reconstruction:
The Senate text struck only section 1 of the House bill, inserted a new Division A concerning Russia sanctions and Iran-sanctions authorization, and added a Division B heading before retained House section 2. The retained provision extends the educator-expense deduction to qualifying early-childhood educators for expenses in tax years after 2025. The new sanctions cover specified Russian persons, banks, vessels, energy and related transactions, with import duties, waivers, congressional review and termination provisions. Section 114(a) exempts medicines, medical devices, humanitarian assistance and related transactions from Title I measures; it also addresses covered international agreements with Ukraine subject to a presidential sanctions-evasion determination. Section 114(e) separately excepts low-enriched uranium or medical isotopes imported under the specified statutory waiver. These are conditions on medical-supply transactions within a sanctions package, not a new domestic health benefit. Section 201 extends the Iran Sanctions Act expiration to 2031, while section 203 sunsets the other new authorities after five years.

The exact choice on September 16, 2026 is one motion to concur in all Senate amendments to H.R.5334 under H.Res.1530 section 5. It is not a new vote solely on the educator-deduction title, a vote on each sanction or a judgment about any person's conduct. Whole Senate EAS and retained House section 2 are read; the rule prohibits division of this concurrence question. The literal floor/EAS comparison retains its two template differences: section '__' versus extracted 'll' and date '___' versus 'lll'. Both versions explicitly call these blanks to be filled with a section number and date; other letters and digits match after declared bounded formatting normalization. Literal sources remain unchanged and no universal punctuation/PDF-glyph equivalence is claimed.

The Immigration relationship is directly grounded in section 102(e)(2). Subject to its covered-person predicates and title exceptions, an alien described in 102(b) is inadmissible, ineligible for a visa or other entry documentation, admission or parole, and any other INA benefit. Existing visas or entry documents are revoked regardless of issuance date; revocation takes effect immediately and automatically cancels other valid visas or entry documents possessed by that alien. This is not a removal order, a citizenship revocation or a finding that every Russian national is covered. Section 102 requires presidential review within 30 days and every 180 days thereafter, with determinations under the printed official, conduct, ownership, vessel/port, evasion and transferred-property branches. Knowing includes actual knowledge or should-have-known. Vessel blocking is distinct from alien eligibility; vessels are not persons eligible for visas. Source characterizations and allegations are conditions in the proposal, not adopted personal findings.

Section 101's alien means neither a US citizen nor a US national. Admission is lawful entry after inspection and authorization; parole and temporary crew landing are not admission, and the retained LPR admission exceptions remain separate. United States person in this title includes US citizens, LPR aliens and domestic-law entities including foreign branches. Foreign person is its complement, while Russian person separately includes Russian citizens/nationals and specified entities. Thus alien and foreign person are not interchangeable: the new sanctions do not infer one uniform nationality or immigration-status rule. Title restrictions on US-person transactions or investments retain that explicit defined scope without deciding an individual's or entity's qualification.

Section 103(a)(1)(C) directs use of the 102(e) consequences with respect to the named bank leaders, officials, executives, board members and controlling/majority shareholders. Section 108(b) incorporates that menu for foreign persons that the President determines knowingly provide specified support facilitating maintenance or expansion of production of the listed energy products for use by any person subject to sanctions under 102 or 103; section 111(b) incorporates it for the named Rosatom leadership/shareholder classes. Their printed imported subject and consequence language is preserved without silently rewriting 102(e)'s own 'alien described in subsection (b)' text or deciding any individual cross-application. Separately, 103(d)(2) uses two or more not-already-imposed CAATSA235 sanctions. The dated 9529 menu includes discretionary corporate-officer visa denial/exclusion and a principal-executive-officer branch; selecting a menu does not establish that every optional visa sanction is imposed.

The wider package also includes specified property blocking, financial-account/transaction restrictions, licensing-qualified transfer restrictions, securities exchange prohibitions, investment/service restrictions, sovereign-debt restrictions and a separate international financial-messaging mechanism with its own qualified waiver. Entity affiliation or property in US-person custody is not itself a visa-status judgment. Section 112 increases Russian-origin import duties to up to 500 percent, additional to other duties. Section 113's distinct up-to-100-percent duties are confined to its printed country tests, with top-five, volume-period, post-enactment purchase, sanctions-evasion and natural-gas qualifications. Section 113(b) requires the US Trade Representative's written determination for a modified rate greater than zero and up to 100 percent; 113(g) requires the President or Trade Representative's justification/methodology report at least ten days before imposition or modification, and 113(e) requires the Trade Representative's first review within 180 days of initial duties and every 180 days thereafter. Those distinct obligations remain; this is not a tariff on every country, a mandatory maximum rate or an inferred effect on prices or persons.

Section 114 retains separately scoped humanitarian transactions and related transactions, intelligence/law-enforcement activities, admission/parole necessary for international obligations including the named UN-headquarters and consular agreements, civilian nuclear-cooperation agreements, qualified uranium/medical-isotope imports, official government/UN business, non-Russian transit oil, prior general licences, the 270-day winddown conditions, vessel/crew safety and NASA/non-DoD launch provisions. The retained treaty claim is the bill's own conditional exception, not an independent interpretation of either agreement. Section 114(c) names the UN Headquarters agreement signed June 26, 1947 and entered into force November 21, 1947, and the Convention on Consular Relations done April 24, 1963 and entered into force March 19, 1967, as printed. It excepts admission or parole only when necessary to comply with US obligations under those agreements or other international obligations. It does not expressly turn this exception into a general exemption from every visa, document-revocation or INA-benefit consequence. Treaty reservations, amendments, US-specific treaty applicability and any individual necessary-to-comply determination remain unresolved legal applications for review, rather than new eligibility findings. The dated law/order witnesses establish only the stated baseline propositions; they do not establish a future enactment-day EO inventory, any issued licence or uninterrupted operation. No newly searched treaty text is used as a governed claim source. The admission/parole obligation predicate is preserved; this candidate does not decide the relevant underlying obligation, treaty date, diplomatic class or individual right. It does not convert every exception into a universal visa/document/benefit entitlement. Uranium 111(b) starts at the specifically referenced statutory waiver-termination date: the dated 2297h-10a(d)(2)(C) says no later than January 1, 2028, distinct from its December 31, 2040 statutory end. Actual waiver inventories and other-law transaction authority are not certified.

Section 115 permits qualified presidential waiver of sanctions, restrictions or duties with written national-interest certification and explanatory report before issuance; same-section reports may be consolidated, unclassified with classified annex permitted. Its duty-rate-report exception does not negate 113(b)'s written determination or 113(g)(1)'s report. Section 117 termination requires the printed written certifications for Russian versus other foreign persons/countries, including peace/cessation or cessation/reliable-assurance predicates. Termination waits 30 calendar days for congressional review, or 60 days for reports submitted July 10 through September 7 inclusive; disapproval must be enacted, not merely introduced or passed by one chamber. The expedited procedures and Senate three-fifths thresholds remain distinct from the vote on this package. Section 116 retains named implementation authorities and qualified civil/criminal violation penalties; no actual enforcement or guilt is inferred.

Section 102(d) preserves specified harmful-foreign-activity EO measures as in effect the day before enactment. Original issued EO versions are historical witnesses, not a complete current or future enactment-day inventory. The March 24, 2026 continuation notice expressly names eight orders, including the later14114,14329and14384. Their captured issued bodies are retained:14114 adds foreign-financial-institution and import mechanisms to the earlier framework;14329 imposes qualified additional India-import duties, and14384 removes those additional duties from February7,2026under its own qualifications and monitoring. The earlier imposed duty is not presented as an unchanged current rule; executive characterizations are attributed. Product customs/foreign-trade-zone status is not personal immigration status. These witnesses still do not certify a future enactment-day inventory or actual licences, judicial application or individual cases. General-licence and other existing-law predicates remain conditional. Section 201 extends the dated Iran Act's December 31, 2026 endpoint to 2031; it is exempted from the separate five-year Division A sunset in 203. Retained House section 2 adds qualifying early-childhood teachers and specified facilities to the educator-expense deduction for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025; it does not independently establish Immigration membership or a personal tax eligibility finding.

A Yea supports, and a Nay opposes, the whole concurrence; neither identifies a separate component position, preferred alternative or motive. Concurrence is a House outcome, not proof of enactment or implementation. Candidate screening is recorded using the original unapproved shared candidate identity, meaning prefix, witnesses and limits. Independent source/domain review and editorial acceptance remain pending; no publication authorization or individual legal finding is conferred.

exact_identity.vote-desc: Ukraine Support Act

substantive_actions.primary_reconstruction:
The exact June4 final-passage question concerned the complete H.R.2913EH Ukraine Support Act, considered under H.Res.518, not the separate discharge or consideration votes. Proposed Health membership rests on operative medical-isotope, medicine/device/food and humanitarian-assistance rules, not war-related hospital/hunger findings or a forecast that military support would improve health. It is a broad three-title foreign-policy/security/economic package with discrete Health mechanisms and limitations. Author the shared whole-package meaning once and project the actual votes mechanically.

Section307would impose specified Rosatom sanctions under the title's qualifying Russian-war/negotiation/peace-agreement trigger. Its medical AND industrial isotope transaction waiver is DISCRETIONARY: the President must determine that the transaction relates to activities necessary to produce medical or industrial isotopes, certify that domestic medical or industrial isotope production is insufficient to meet United States patient and industry requirements, AND certify measurable steps toward medical or industrial isotope supply chains independent of Rosatom or other Russian source material. It is not an automatic exception for every medical transaction, a general exemption for nuclear fuel or a guarantee of isotope supply. The surrounding sanctions have diplomatic triggers, termination/reimposition and congressional-review rules; do not erase them based on a nuclear-supply warning in debate.

Section313would impose the defined foreign-direct-product export/reexport/in-country transfer licensing rule for covered UStechnology/software-dependent items and plants/components destined forRussia or specified knowledge of incorporation/use. Its food, medicine and medical-device license exception applies to EAR99items OR items not listed on the Commerce Control List. It does not exempt every medicine/device regardless of classification or license conditions. Section319(a)(2)separately prohibits TITLEIII SANCTIONS on transactions for sale of agricultural commodities, food, medicine or medical devices; humanitarian assistance; and related financial transactions/facilitation. That limit does not automatically lift all other Russia restrictions, tariffs, taxes or export controls. Existing50usc1702(b)(2)already protects specified donations of articles such as food/clothing/medicine subject to its emergency/coercion/armed-forces exceptions. The new transaction rule is not represented as the first humanitarian exception in law, and the older donation exception is not generalized to every commercial export.

Section110would establish a Ukraine Reconstruction Trust Fund and appropriate amounts equivalent to net revenues of taxes under the printed26usc892A reference. Funds are available to State AS PROVIDED IN APPROPRIATION ACTS only for reconstruction, humanitarian assistance, economic growth/private-enterprise/governance assistance inUkraine, subject to applicable Foreign Assistance Act requirements and notification/reporting. The text also imposes yearly reporting for the stated period. This is qualified humanitarian/reconstruction authority, not an identified hospital grant, guaranteed fund receipts or guaranteed food/medical delivery. The EH does not create the cited892Asection. Its separate section316sets a100percent tax on interest/dividends received from USblocked Russian/Belarusian-government assets, despite the heading's capital-gains wording. Do not silently equate that free-standing tax with the printed892Arevenue reference or repair the fund's funding link. The mismatch remains an express candidate qualification; no invented revenue estimate or claimed operative funding source is accepted.

Section104addsUkraine to the DFCcountry-priority framework and exempts the specified upper-middle-income country certification requirements. Existing22usc9612(c)otherwise prioritizes less-developed countries and gives defined conditions for upper-middle-income assistance. This is not universal Ukrainian medical coverage or a new unconditional household grant. War-risk cargo insurance and the grain-shipping insurance initiative are broader economic mechanisms, not proof that food assistance reached beneficiaries. Other titleIparts include reconstruction coordination, Radio Free Europe authorization, disinformation programs and a$30million annual nuclear-cooperation authorization for fiscal2025–2029. An authorization/backdated fiscal label does not show an actual appropriation or nuclear-care outcome.

The whole package also extends lend-lease through2028, provides the specified$8billion conditional military-financing loan authority and related unobligated-fund provisions, authorizes Baltic military/demining funds and Ukraine security assistance, and requires military/intelligence reports. TitleIIIincludes financial/debt/oil/gas/shadow-fleet/SWIFT/Rosatom/official/child-deportation sanctions, refinery-import limits,500percent tariffs and blocked-asset tax measures, with specified extraordinary-national-interest waivers, notification/congressional review, termination and possible reimposition. Printed internal cross-references in financial/strategy provisions remain as written rather than being silently corrected or projected as guaranteed implementation. Conditional exceptions in307,313and319retain their own distinct scope; no claim that all trade/finance becomes prohibited or exempt follows.

Floor supporters described aid, deterrence and negotiation benefits. floor opponents criticized stale provisions, draft errors, mandatory restrictions, nuclear supply and an alternative sanctions strategy. Those are attributed arguments, not observed effects, established motives or preferred alternatives assigned to either member. The actual operative exceptions and funding mismatch qualify both sides' broad rhetoric. The final question passed226–195with9Not Voting. A Yea supports and a Nay opposes this exact whole foreign-policy/security/assistance package. These package directions do not establish separate positions on every humanitarian or medical exception, endorsement of a war strategy, enactment, medical delivery or future outcomes.

The Immigration relationship is the explicit section317(2) operator, not a general inference from war, nationality, humanitarian assistance or foreign policy. In the case of an alien to whom the specified sanctions apply, the proposal makes the alien inadmissible and ineligible for a visa or other entry documentation, admission or parole, or any other benefit under the Immigration and Nationality Act. An existing visa or entry document is revoked regardless of when issued; revocation takes effect immediately and automatically cancels other valid visas or entry documents possessed by the alien. These are conditional proposed consequences, not a finding that a named individual qualifies, a removal order, citizenship revocation or an enacted outcome. Section317(1)'s property blocking and317(3)'s direction to US international-financial-institution executive directors remain distinct from317(2)'s alien operator. A vessel or corporate entity is not thereby an alien eligible for a visa.

Section322 imports alien/admission/admitted from INA101: alien means neither a US citizen nor a US national; lawful admission requires inspection and authorization, while parole and temporary crew landing are not admission. The dated8usc1101 witness retains the LPR return/admission exceptions and definition; it is bounded context, not the entire INA or an individual classifier. United States person separately includes US citizens, LPR aliens and domestic-law entities, including foreign branches. Foreign person is the complement of that definition. These categories are not interchangeable: LPR aliens can be US persons, and not every Russian citizen or national is automatically a covered alien under this bill. Knowing includes actual knowledge or should-have-known. Section322's financial-institution reference is its specified31usc5312 subset and foreign-financial-institution definition imports Treasury regulations; no particular institution's qualification, live regulatory inventory or individual status is decided.

Section301 requires the initial presidential determination within15days after enactment and, as printed, 'at minimum every90days thereafter'. Its three alternative predicates concern continued war of aggression, refusal sincerely and actually to negotiate a peace agreement, or violation of such an agreement. Section322 defines war of aggression using the specified ground/amphibious/airborne assaults, blockades, drone/missile attacks or cyber operations with physical repercussions within the preceding30days. The proposal's characterizations are conditions or attributed legislative findings, not new factual findings about individuals. An affirmative determination and the relevant timing/target predicates remain material; the candidate does not claim sanctions already imposed.

Direct printed317 routes include302(a)(1)'s sanctions on three or more named financial institutions within15days after the affirmative301determination;303's specified Russian energy/mineral companies;304(a)'s listed or additionally included officials;305's knowing Crimea bridge/tunnel construction, maintenance or repair;306's specified Zaporizhzhia endangerment/control conduct with its Ukrainian-control-restoration exception;307's Rosatom/subsidiary and knowing significant reactor transaction branches with the separate isotope waiver;308's foreign vessels knowingly transporting oil contrary to the price-cap condition with crew/life/vessel/environmental safety qualifications;309's financial-messaging-service condition;311's distinct North Korea cooperation, responsible-person, knowing/significant-transaction and logistical-support branches; and312's directed/participated kidnapping and wrongful printed 'patriation' of Ukrainian children. Each keeps its own affirmative301/15-day, covered-subject and other conditions. Direct references to the317menu do not erase its alien-specific wording or resolve every cross-subject application; individual, vessel, entity and institution consequences remain distinct. No personal allegation is adopted and no official or company is newly designated by this candidate.

The malformed routes are preserved separately. Section302(a)(2) says the President MAY impose 'section310(a)(1)' sanctions on subsidiaries/successors, although310's printed sovereign-debt body has no(a)(1). Section302(b)'s additional financial-institution list is due within30days and every90days, requires ownership OR operation by the Russian government AND the presidential national-security determination, and its follow-on also says310(a)(1). Section304(c) refers to officials' operations 'described in section302', and its follow-on sanctions say310, while304(a) separately says317. Section310 itself requires its affirmative determination 'under section302', not301, and governs US-person transactions in Russian sovereign debt issued on/after enactment within its30-day timing. Section308(d)'s strategy reference says(a) although the strategy appears in(c). These literal mismatches, the trust-fund892A/316 mismatch, and other printed internal references remain unresolved legal questions; the candidate neither substitutes317/301 nor invents repaired subdivisions, targets or implementation.

Section319(a)(1) excepts317(2) sanctions 'with respect to admission' if admitting OR paroling the alien is necessary to comply with US obligations under the UN Headquarters Agreement signed June26,1947and entered into force November21,1947, or other applicable international obligations. This claim states the bill's conditional exception. It does not independently interpret the underlying agreement, reservations or later amendments, confer a personal treaty entitlement, or convert an admission/parole predicate into an express blanket visa/document-revocation or all-INA-benefit exemption. Those applications remain for legal review. Section319(a)(2) separately bars TitleIII sanctions on transactions or their facilitation for the sale of agricultural commodities, food, medicine or medical devices; OR provision of humanitarian assistance; OR financial transactions relating to humanitarian assistance. The last financing branch is expressly tied to humanitarian assistance, not a blanket financial-transaction exemption. Section319(a)(3) separately excepts authorized US intelligence, law-enforcement or national-security activities. A financial or travel transaction exception does not itself grant entry permission. Section319(b)'s presidential waiver remains discretionary, subject to the printed national-security determination and reasons report at least15days before exercise. Its grammatical wording 'such a waiver is in the extraordinarily vital to the national security of the United States' remains as printed, without repair or a claimed waiver in force.

Section 318(a) permits the President to exercise the specified IEEPA 203/205 implementation authorities; 318(b) requires the President to issue regulations, licences and orders necessary to carry out the title; 318(c) imports 206(b)/(c) penalties for violations as printed. Dated1702retains temporal/jurisdictional predicates and the distinct personal-communication, qualified donation, information and travel-transaction exceptions;1704and1705supply the bounded regulation/penalty witnesses. No guilt, actual enforcement, adjusted current civil-penalty amount or universal exemption is inferred. The wider package retains313's product AND destination licensing scope and classification-qualified food/medicine/device exception;314's Russian-origin goods/services duty is NOT LESS THAN500percent, rather than a500percent maximum. Section316's100percent tax is on the defined interest/dividend income from blocked Russian/Belarusian-government assets, not all capital gains or an automatic cure for110's892Afunding reference. These trade/tax and humanitarian provisions do not independently decide personal immigration eligibility.

Section320permits termination only with its certification to Congress that Russia has ceased the specified war of aggression or printed peace-agreement violation condition; it requires immediate reimposition if the specified conduct restarts. Section321separately requires a proposed-action/reasons report for covered termination, person-waiver or significant-foreign-policy licensing actions. Its listed source framework includes this Act and the named executive orders13849,13883,14024,14039,14065,14066,14068,14071and14114; this is a description of321's printed coverage, not a certificate of every order's current operation, complete contents, amendment chain or an enactment-day/licence inventory. Routine licences that do not significantly alter US foreign policy are qualified separately. The report distinguishes intended significant policy alteration and required matters, with confidentiality safeguards. Review is ordinarily30calendar days, or60for reports submitted July10through September7inclusive. The President cannot take the proposed action during review absent an enacted approval resolution; a covered joint resolution of disapproval passing both Houses in accordance with 321(c) prohibits the proposed action for 12 calendar days after the date of passage. If that covered resolution passes both Houses under 321(c) and the President vetoes it, the President may not take the proposed action for 10 calendar days after the date of the President's veto. These event-anchored periods are not automatically cumulative extensions; enacted disapproval prohibits the action. The expedited resolution and chamber procedures, Senate debate/appeal/revenue-companion distinctions and no-tolling rule remain; they are not new votes on each sanction. No three-fifths threshold from a different bill is imported.

A Yea supports and a Nay opposes passing this exact whole H.R.2913EH package. The House's passage and these mechanically projected official observations establish no separate position on a visa sanction, humanitarian exception, named person, treaty or preferred alternative. The original unapproved Health shared identity, meaning prefix, witnesses and limits remain intact; this source-qualified Immigration augmentation records candidate screening only. Independent source/domain review and editorial acceptance remain pending. No publication authorization, current-law consolidation, individual legal application or production action is conferred.

exact_identity.vote-desc: Making continuing appropriations for fiscal year 2027, and for other purposes

substantive_actions.primary_reconstruction:
The exact July 21 final-passage proposition is the whole H.R. 9770 continuing-appropriations package for FY 2027. Section 101 continues otherwise unprovided FY 2026 projects/activities, including direct-loan/guarantee costs, at the prior operational rates and under the incorporated authorities and conditions from twelve specified appropriations divisions. These include HHS, Interior/IHS, Agriculture/FDA, VA and HUD alongside defense, homeland-security, diplomatic and other appropriations. The direct clinical/social funding nexus is established by the referenced medical-care appropriations and the bill's explicit IHS, WIC, mandatory-benefit and TANF mechanisms, not by assuming every federal operation is healthcare. This is a whole-package vote, not separate positions on each incorporated program or rider.

Unless otherwise provided, the ordinary availability ends at the earliest of a project appropriation's enactment, a relevant FY 2027 Act omitting it, or December 4, 2026. The bill preserves conditions of the pertinent Acts, restricts new/unfunded activities and certain defense production/procurement, limits high initial distributions and requires only the most limited continuation funding action. Expenditures are charged to later applicable enacted appropriations. The apportionment-timing waiver does not waive every apportionment law. Rescissions/cancellations continue with specified account/rate treatment and the lesser-of-stated-amount/October 1 balances limit, not an invented universal cancellation. Emergency/disaster designations are budget treatment, not independent benefit eligibility.

Section 111 continues covered entitlements/mandatory payments and Food and Nutrition Act activities at current-law program levels and applicable FY 2026 conditions through December 4. Its separately stated authority for mandatory payments due on/about the first day of a month after October 2026 and not later than 30 days after December 4 does not extend every discretionary account by 30 days or create SNAP eligibility. Section 116 permits WIC apportionment at the rate needed to maintain participation; that is an operational authority, not an expansion of eligibility or guarantee against every disruption. Sections 112/122/125 permit qualified personnel, FEMAdisaster-response/recovery and wildfire operational apportionment; the personnel authority follows necessary nonpersonnel expense reductions and is not a promise of no furloughs.

Section 123 adds IHS operational rates of 75.774 million for services and 8.296 million for facilities to staff/operate facilities opened, renovated or expanded in FY 2022, 2026 or 2027, with permitted necessary apportionment. These are rates during the CR window, not proof of a full 83-million disbursement or new entitlement. Existing PL 119-74 already provides separate FY 2027 IHS advance appropriations with specified availability, use and administrative conditions. PL 119-75 also already supplies first-quarter FY 2027 Medicaid authority. Those existing advances must not be represented as newly created by this CR or added again to its two specified IHS rates.

Section 126 continues SSA part A/title IV activities, except 403(c) and 418, and 1108(b) territorial activities in the FY 2026 manner through December 4, appropriating necessary sums. Existing PL 119-75 section 6304 already continues the specified TANF activities through December 31, 2026. This CR does not expressly repeal or shorten that later existing authority. The cited 403(c) is pandemic emergency assistance under the governed 2024 Code, not the ordinary 403(b) Contingency Fund. Section 418 is separately appropriated childcare assistance; excluding it from this particular extension is not a repeal of all childcare funding or a universal claim that the ordinary TANF contingency fund ends. The dated pandemic assistance has its own use/expenditure boundaries, not a new FY 2027 pandemic allocation.

Incorporated existing HHSconditions include the qualified abortion/coverage funding restrictions with rape, incest and physician-certified life-endangerment exceptions; separate State/local/private funds and Medicaid-match limits; defined health-entity nondiscrimination terms; embryo-research restrictions and defined clinical-evidence/trial exceptions to the drug-legalization promotion restriction. Title Xvoluntary-family-planning funds retain nondirective pregnancy counseling and their own abortion-use restriction. Continuation is not unrestricted new health spending or repeal of these conditions.

Other exact provisions retain their scopes. Section 124 extends the application of specified wildland-firefighter premium-pay treatment to calendar years 2021 through 2026; PL 117-43 title VII 1701 is not Afghan refugee eligibility. Its aggregate executive pay cap and exclusion from basic-pay retirement/leave calculations remain. Section 120 modifies the referenced political-appointee pay limitation, not a universal freeze for medical staff. The DCclause permits local-fund spending at its specified local-budget rate; it is not a new Federal medical appropriation. Flood-insurance date changes retain their immediate/retroactive effective condition. Agricultural market reporting, SBA financing, Congress pay and specified survivor payments remain package components. H. Res. 1438's conditional SAVE engrossment applies to H.R. 8800, not this CR; no election division is invented here.

Supporters described continuity and avoidance of disruption; opponents disputed the package's sufficiency, missing housing/utility adjustments and DHS provisions. These arguments are attributed rather than treated as proof of uninterrupted services, wrongdoing, actual funding transfers or voters' reasons. Yea supports this exact temporary combined package and Nay opposes it. Neither supplies independent positions on every healthcare, nutrition, housing or enforcement component, a preferred alternative, an implemented shutdown outcome or enactment.

This is ordinary final passage of the complete H.R.9770EH, not suspension, a vote on H.R.8800, or a separately adopted SAVE division. The own callup/initial voice-aye/demand-order/postponement/resumed vote remains bound, with220-205and6NotVoting. H.Res1438's conditional SAVE treatment belongs to8800, not9770. Section106(3)'s ordinary backstop is December4,2026;111(b)'s first-of-month payments remain separately qualified. Section101(6) names ONLY divisionA of PL11986. It does not expressly add5013-5016of PL11975, and the broader H.R.6500Senate language is not substituted into this earlier House choice. The direct DHS continuing-funding mechanisms above, subject to the literal divisionA and permanent-law conditions, support Immigration candidate membership without a claim of unrestricted programme extension or resolved annual-date/application questions.

The complete original Health account remains: IHS operational rates are distinct from existing advances, WIC participation apportionment is qualified, and section126's TANF December4window does not expressly repeal the already specified December31authority. Its exceptions are403(c)pandemic assistance and418childcare, not all contingency/childcare support. Section124's1701reference is wildfire-worker premium pay, not refugee eligibility. The preserved twelve-appropriation list, no-new-activity conditions, rescissions and authority limits remain; no complete current-law or guaranteed-services certificate is inferred. Yea supports and Nay opposes passing this whole exact CR, without a separate immigration, health, fiscal or preferred-alternative position.

The Immigration relationship rests on the literal temporary-funding operators and the imported, directly identified immigration administration and border activities, not the generic title or an inference that every department programme has an Immigration purpose. Section101 continues only qualifying projects/activities conducted in fiscal2026, at the specified operational rates and under the referenced authority and conditions, unless otherwise provided. Sections102-104 retain defence/new-activity restrictions;103 retains the extent/manner of the pertinent appropriation. Section106 ends ordinary availability at the earliest applicable replacement appropriation, applicable fiscal2027Act omitting the project/activity, or the specified December date, unless otherwise provided. Sections108-110 concern apportionment timing, restrictions on early distributions/grants impinging on final funding prerogatives, and the most limited permissible funding action. Section108 does not waive other apportionment law. Section111's distinct mandatory first-of-month payment timing is not a uniform extra30days for every agency, project or entitlement. Section112's personnel apportionment requires necessary non-personnel expense reductions/deferrals first; actual furloughs, sufficient funding or service continuity are not established.

The complete preserved PL11986 witness separates its preliminary section4, divisionA's direct DHS appropriations and divisionB. Its explanatory-statement exception covers contents under ICE and CBP Border Security Operations and the corresponding amounts in the specified FinalBill column entries; it does not zero all CBP appropriations or all immigration funding. The candidate relies on the literal direct appropriation/operator branches and retains the distinction between divisionA-only incorporation and the broader outer-Act reference. It does not certify every explanatory-table allocation, reset every fiscal2026date or resolve all preliminary/inside-division cross-reference applications. A baseline annual amount is a rate reference, not a new full annual payment or a second copy of an existing advance.

Direct DHS branches include CBP Operations and Support's necessary expenses including transportation of unaccompanied alien minors; air and marine support to Federal, State, local and international agencies in the enforcement or administration of laws enforced by DHS; and, at the Secretary's discretion, such air and marine support to Federal, State and local agencies in other law-enforcement and emergency humanitarian efforts; USCIS Operations and Support's122.941million annual baseline INCLUDING E-Verify, not a122.941million earmark solely for E-Verify, additive to other funds without a required8USC1356(m)fee reduction; and the specified immigration-officer competition and supervised biometrics provisions. They do not make every DHS dollar an immigration-enforcement dollar or grant anyone admission, work permission or a benefit. Section204's land-border fee prohibition concerns new crossing fees and the specified studies for pedestrians, cyclists, drivers or passengers in private vehicles at northern/southern land ports; it is not a ban on every passport, air or maritime fee. Baseline527retains specific pregnancy/post-delivery custody/transport restraint conditions, exceptions, least-restrictive/medical safeguards and absolute labour/delivery restraints; this vote does not supply a medical finding or authorize unrestricted restraint.

Sections537and538retain monthly planning estimates and independent validation rather than findings of actual arrivals, guilt, detention or removals. Their current/following-fiscal-year, demographic, budget/reporting and503reprogramming-suspension conditions remain.537shares arrival estimates with HHS, Attorney General, State and appropriators;538's printed recipients are Attorney General, State and appropriators, without importing HHS into that separate clause. Specific DHS budget and legislative conditions remain distinct from personal immigration classification. No rule that every funded benefit programme ignores its permanent eligibility statutes, or that all noncitizens qualify or are excluded, is proposed.

The whole multi-domain choice retains all original unapproved Health shared identity, meaning prefix, source witnesses and limitations. Those qualified Health mechanisms and original source readings are preserved and attributed, not newly recertified as every underlying agency law. Immigration augmentation establishes a defensible source-grounded candidate from the direct mechanisms while reserving full fiscal/current-law integration, explanatory/recipient-table and individual/legal applications. No separate component stance, motive, enactment, implementation, editorial acceptance or publication follows from House passage. Independent source/domain review remains pending.

exact_identity.vote-question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in the Senate Amendments
exact_identity.vote-desc: AGOA Extension Act

substantive_actions.primary_reconstruction:
The Senate amendments replaced H.R.6500’s earlier trade-extension text with a multi-domain continuing-appropriations and extensions package. DivisionA generally continued specified fiscal 2026 activities at prior rates until the earliest applicable appropriation event or December 11, 2026, subject to its restrictions and exceptions. DivisionD extended certain veterans’ nursing-home, mental-health, suicide-prevention, ambulance-reimbursement and other care authorities to December 11, 2026, with specified funding amounts and separate housing/benefits provisions. Section 2007 reduced the Medicare Improvement Fund amount from $2.062 billion to $2.041 billion. The package also included authorizing, trade and surface-transportation extensions. The question combined suspension of the rules with concurrence in the complete Senate replacement.

This is the whole Senate replacement for H.R.6500, with four divisions, under suspension and concurrence in Senate amendments and its two-thirds procedure. The Senate strikes the House text after the enacting clause and replaces its title; the old House trade-only proposal is not substituted for the recorded choice. The own motion, initial voice result/demand/order/postponement and resumed370-48with14NotVoting remain separate. Section3normally makes 'this Act' division-local unless expressly otherwise provided. DivisionA106(3)uses December11,2026, not the earlier9770December4endpoint.101(6)names PL11986 EXCEPT divisionB and expressly includes PL11975divisionI5013-5016, unlike9770's divisionA-only reference. Literal scope and preliminary-section4applications remain qualified, not silently homogenized.

The referenced5013-5015say to apply their specified printed2015dates as September30,2026for the J-physician220(c), IIRIRA401(b)and non-minister religious-worker101(a)(27)(C)(ii)routes. The dated1182(e)/1184(l), IIRIRA401-405and complete selected27(C)witnesses retain their programme predicates. J-physician hardship/persecution/agency recommendation, public-interest and applicable service/State-number conditions are not a universal waiver. IIRIRA's printed pilot-program structure and voluntary-election exceptions are not proof that all three historical pilots are currently operating or that every employer is newly mandated.27(C)'s denomination membership and continuous work periods, bona fide/nonprofit organization, specified vocation/occupation and accompanying/following spouse/children conditions remain, while its minister branch lacks those two printed non-minister sunset dates. No individual affiliation, petition, job or immigration status is decided. The imported5013-5015date events are distinct:220(c)concerns admission in J status or acquisition of that status after admission; IIRIRA401(b)concerns programme termination; and27(C)(ii)(II)-(III)concern the specified non-minister entry before the applicable date. The J cutoff is not a universal expiration of previously granted waivers. Including these fiscal2026clauses in101does not itself establish a newly rewritten December11or fiscal2027application for those different events; their annual/current-law applications remain unresolved rather than silently repaired.

5016requires the DHS Secretary, AFTER consultation with Labor AND a determination that fiscal2026US-business needs cannot be met by willing, qualified and able US workers, and says MAY increase H-2Bnumbers by NOT MORE THAN the highest number of returning-worker programme participants in any year when they were cap-exempt. The underlying1184(g)H-2B numerical rules, including the g(1)(B)66,000principal cap and family distinction, remain separate from1184(l)'s J-physician waiver, service, State-number and related conditions. This is not an automatic unlimited increase, a selected2021-2025returner cohort, a calculated new cap or proof of a fiscal2027increase; the printed fiscal-year and current-application questions stay unresolved.

DivisionB2013expressly applies6USC348(b)(13)with December11,2026in place of September30,2026. The dated(b)(13)says THIS SECTION expires; the scope is not reduced to subsectionb. The baseline provides discretionary joint task forces for purposes that are or relate to securing the land and maritime borders, homeland-security crises, or establishing regionally-based operations. These are three establishment/operation categories; the separate other-duties clause concerns the Director. Appointment/personnel/command, Coast Guard/FEMA and oversight/reporting limits remain, including the separate Stafford/FEMA-response restriction and its stated conditions. This prolongs the specified section-wide authority on the proposal's terms, not a finding that a task force is established, deployed or effective.2017strikes the printed September30,2010date in22USC214(b)(2)for December11,2026. The dated214witness already notes PL1172639802(a)'s September30,2026application, so this is not described as the first-ever surcharge or proof of a lapse since2010. The discretionary/regulatory, additive fee and consular/border-security-account purposes remain qualified by the witness's amendments/notes; no live fee schedule or individual's actual charge is certified.2016's international religious freedom commission is distinct from5015non-minister visas.

Other divisionBextensions remain in the whole choice: grain/Forest/food assistance, DPA, TSCA fees, NMI Medicaid amount, AGOA/Haiti preferences, customs/merchandise fees, cybersecurity, technology and patent fees, Medicare Fund reduction and scorekeeping rules. Scorecard classification is not zero actual cost.2019until December11limits PL11937divisionB781amendments ONLY to the two specified intermediate/final-product categories containing cannabinoids not capable of natural production by Cannabis sativa L.; it does not cancel every hemp amendment or equate natural production with all safety/legality. The existing complete781witness retains its own365-day effective date, other exclusions, amounts and definitions. No immigration/drug-inadmissibility classification is decided from that product clause.

DivisionC's covered-law extension applies to provisions that otherwise expire September30,2026, with its defined October1-December11period and day/365fraction. Highway/MassTransitTrust amounts are EQUAL to that fraction; specified general/other funding is NOT LESS THAN it. It does not renew every transportation or licensing rule indiscriminately.3104's selected unobligated funds remain available through September30,2027, while3201's trust-fund expenditure date is December12, notDecember11. DivisionDretains the complete VA care, benefits, housing and other extenders, with their authorizations, conditions and date exceptions; plot-allowance timing likewise uses December12. Neither division makes new universal veteran, housing, nationality or personal-benefit findings. Yea supports and Nay opposes this whole replacement/suspension-concurrence choice, not separate component choices.

The Immigration relationship rests on the literal temporary-funding operators and the imported, directly identified immigration administration and border activities, not the generic title or an inference that every department programme has an Immigration purpose. Section101 continues only qualifying projects/activities conducted in fiscal2026, at the specified operational rates and under the referenced authority and conditions, unless otherwise provided. Sections102-104 retain defence/new-activity restrictions;103 retains the extent/manner of the pertinent appropriation. Section106 ends ordinary availability at the earliest applicable replacement appropriation, applicable fiscal2027Act omitting the project/activity, or the specified December date, unless otherwise provided. Sections108-110 concern apportionment timing, restrictions on early distributions/grants impinging on final funding prerogatives, and the most limited permissible funding action. Section108 does not waive other apportionment law. Section111's distinct mandatory first-of-month payment timing is not a uniform extra30days for every agency, project or entitlement. Section112's personnel apportionment requires necessary non-personnel expense reductions/deferrals first; actual furloughs, sufficient funding or service continuity are not established.

The complete preserved PL11986 witness separates its preliminary section4, divisionA's direct DHS appropriations and divisionB. Its explanatory-statement exception covers contents under ICE and CBP Border Security Operations and the corresponding amounts in the specified FinalBill column entries; it does not zero all CBP appropriations or all immigration funding. The candidate relies on the literal direct appropriation/operator branches and retains the distinction between divisionA-only incorporation and the broader outer-Act reference. It does not certify every explanatory-table allocation, reset every fiscal2026date or resolve all preliminary/inside-division cross-reference applications. A baseline annual amount is a rate reference, not a new full annual payment or a second copy of an existing advance.

Direct DHS branches include CBP Operations and Support's necessary expenses including transportation of unaccompanied alien minors; air and marine support to Federal, State, local and international agencies in the enforcement or administration of laws enforced by DHS; and, at the Secretary's discretion, such air and marine support to Federal, State and local agencies in other law-enforcement and emergency humanitarian efforts; USCIS Operations and Support's122.941million annual baseline INCLUDING E-Verify, not a122.941million earmark solely for E-Verify, additive to other funds without a required8USC1356(m)fee reduction; and the specified immigration-officer competition and supervised biometrics provisions. They do not make every DHS dollar an immigration-enforcement dollar or grant anyone admission, work permission or a benefit. Section204's land-border fee prohibition concerns new crossing fees and the specified studies for pedestrians, cyclists, drivers or passengers in private vehicles at northern/southern land ports; it is not a ban on every passport, air or maritime fee. Baseline527retains specific pregnancy/post-delivery custody/transport restraint conditions, exceptions, least-restrictive/medical safeguards and absolute labour/delivery restraints; this vote does not supply a medical finding or authorize unrestricted restraint.

Sections537and538retain monthly planning estimates and independent validation rather than findings of actual arrivals, guilt, detention or removals. Their current/following-fiscal-year, demographic, budget/reporting and503reprogramming-suspension conditions remain.537shares arrival estimates with HHS, Attorney General, State and appropriators;538's printed recipients are Attorney General, State and appropriators, without importing HHS into that separate clause. Specific DHS budget and legislative conditions remain distinct from personal immigration classification. No rule that every funded benefit programme ignores its permanent eligibility statutes, or that all noncitizens qualify or are excluded, is proposed.

The whole multi-domain choice retains all original unapproved Health shared identity, meaning prefix, source witnesses and limitations. Those qualified Health mechanisms and original source readings are preserved and attributed, not newly recertified as every underlying agency law. Immigration augmentation establishes a defensible source-grounded candidate from the direct mechanisms while reserving full fiscal/current-law integration, explanatory/recipient-table and individual/legal applications. No separate component stance, motive, enactment, implementation, editorial acceptance or publication follows from House passage. Independent source/domain review remains pending.

exact_identity.vote-desc: Farm, Food, and National Security Act

substantive_actions.primary_reconstruction:
The April30,2026 House question was passage of H.R.7567 as amended,224-200 with6 Not Voting. This is one whole farm/food/rural-development package, including commodity, conservation, credit, trade, forestry, energy, agricultural research, regulation and crop-insurance provisions as well as the Health and social-support mechanisms below. It is not a standalone SNAP or rural-health vote. H.Res.1224 and the April29 Record establish the deemed base as Print119-22 modified by report119-628 PartA; the April30 Record establishes amendment disposition and final passage. The governed EH supplies the operative package text. Its separate adopted hot-chicken and demonstration-report amendments remain individually recorded choices145/146; failed soda amendment151 is not a passed component. Voice/unrecorded amendment outcomes do not create individual member positions. H.Res.1224 section11 orders the Clerk to await H.R.1346 and conditionally append that bill as passed. That prospective engrossment instruction does not establish passage or inclusion of H.R.1346 at this recorded question; no future text is borrowed into this meaning. Subsequent technical engrossment corrections are authorized in the April30 Record, not a separate policy vote.

TitleIV extends or revises household nutrition-assistance programs and administration. Section4102 removes the fiscal2023 sunset on the EBT switching/routing-fee prohibition; the separate interchange-fee bar remains.4103 permits reasonable-cost State contracting for certification/other functions under specified backlog, error-rate or application-increase conditions. It requires merit-principle adherence, no incentives to deny/delay eligible benefits, no contractor financial interest in a retailer, a blended workforce without displacement of merit staff, notification/public information within10days and annual reporting. Its temporary backlog/error-rate expiry conditions and collective-bargaining savings remain. Contracting is permission, not a mandated benefit denial, eligibility reduction or replacement of every State employee.4104 limits the six-month new retailer-application bar to denials on two consecutive occasions within three years; it does not repeal trafficking sanctions generally.4105 adds below-tolerance errors to supplemental reporting without changing the payment-error tolerance calculation.4106/4107 extend printed SNAP/anti-trafficking authority dates to2031.4108 requires proposed EBT security regulations within six months;4109 requires an administrative-cost study within12months. Neither demonstrates deployed protections or reduced costs.

4110 adds animal protein to the incentive-food category within the existing retailer waiver process, retaining the underlying staple-food/current-dietary-recommendation condition and the prohibition on limiting SNAP benefit use. This is an incentive mechanism, not an animal-protein-only benefit or a general food-definition rewrite.4111 moves online purchasing toward a permanent program, with a transition starting within120days and regulations within two years, consumer protections and rural equitable-access considerations.4112 extends food-assistance infrastructure/commodity authorities and permits a State to request up to20percent of its allocated commodity costs through DoD Fresh.4113 extends the Indian-reservation food-procurement demonstration.4114 adds hot rotisserie chicken to2012(k)'s hot-food exceptions, preserving the other conditional meal pathways.4115 requires a feasibility/implementation/effectiveness and recommendation report within120days after ALL food-definition demonstrations conclude; it neither creates demonstration authority nor enacts a food restriction. The failed PartB amendment47 soda exclusion is absent.

4201 retains the senior farmers-market program's mandatory$20.6million annually for2027-2031 and adds maple syrup/tree nuts to the named foods; existing low-income-senior, fresh/local/unprepared-food and benefit-resource/tax protections remain.4202 extends CSFP and creates a delivery pilot with$10million authorized annually for2027-2031, available until spent, with per-State awards capped at the lesser of$4million or the greater of caseload-times$60 and$10,000. Competitive local distribution prioritizes rural areas and permits delivery, staff, transportation and outreach uses. This is not an individual$10million benefit.4204's Tribal CSFP pilot requires$1million appropriated specifically in advance, selection/capacity and procurement conditions, domestic commodities, no material food-package increase and nutrition/Tribal-significance criteria; separate staffing authority is$1.2million annually for2027-2031.4203/4301 extend special nutrition-project and school fresh-produce authorities.

4302 requires at least95percent domestic purchases in EACH designated AMS food category for school food authorities within the retained1760(n) scope, beginning the first school year after enactment. Listed domestically unavailable products are excluded from the calculation; waiver/accommodation authority is restricted. It bars raw/processed poultry and seafood imports from China/Russia. The underlying contiguous-US purchase limitation and separate Hawaii/Puerto Rico rules remain; this is not an unqualified nationwide95percent of all spending rule.4303 preserves GusNIP nutrition incentives and produce-prescription programs, adds all-forms fruit/vegetable priority to incentive grants and broadens produce prescriptions to all forms of fruits, vegetables and legumes. It retains the50percent Federal grant share with existing Tribal matching provisions and adds a discretionary poverty-area waiver. The prescription program still requires a health-care partner and evaluation/coordination conditions. A participant must both be eligible for SNAP benefits or eligible for and enrolled in Medicaid, and belong to a low-income household that has, or is at risk of developing, a diet-related health condition. Printed authorization/administrative dates extend to2031; existing mandatory program amounts are not all replaced or newly appropriated.4305 broadens dairy incentives to qualifying cheese/yogurt and all specified pasteurized vitaminA/D fluid milk varieties, with yogurt added-sugar limits, and raises authorization to$50million available until expended only if appropriated in advance. That is one authorization, not$50million annually or a limit on ordinary SNAP purchases.

4306 authorizes$200million annually for2027-2031 for State/local-farmer food cooperative agreements to procure unprocessed/minimally processed local food and distribute it through proven food-access organizations. Local means within400miles or the defined entity boundaries; at least25percent of annual product value must come from designated small/midsize/beginning/veteran producers. Administrative/technical-assistance caps,10percent Tribal allocation,1percent of the remainder per non-Tribal State and the existing60percent-poverty/40percent-unemployment remainder formula delimit the program.4307 raises Healthy Food Financing's single authorization from$125million to$135million, available until spent, for eligible underserved-area food-retail/enterprise financing rather than direct household cash.4308 replaces the five-year dietary-guideline cycle with a2030 report and at least ten-year intervals, permitting earlier necessary scientific/health updates. The2025 report controls until the first compliant replacement. Independent-board, disclosure, scientific-review and topic-exclusion requirements remain; guidance is not a self-executing SNAP food ban.4309 directs low-risk categorization/regulatory coordination for fresh/raw/minimally processed produce in childcare, with provider compliance/penalty protections and discretionary State-fund withholding.4310 creates practicable common application OR information-sharing and payment-equipment provisions across named SNAP/WIC/farmers-market/Gus programs. Its unrecorded amendment origin does not establish an individual vote on those enrollment provisions.

Rural-care provisions are separate components of the same package.6101 broadens existing temporary telemedicine and community-facility priorities to rural health facilities and mental, behavioral and maternal-health needs, retaining the existing20percent telemedicine set-aside and insufficient-qualified-applicant exception; the printed priority period extends through2027.6102 authorizes$82million annually for2027-2031 for distance learning and telemedicine, with appropriated funds available for the following two fiscal years, not medical-only spending or guaranteed treatment.5107 permits Farm Credit institutions to finance eligible essential community facilities, with a15percent outstanding-loan ceiling and opportunity for other lenders; it is not guaranteed lending.6305 prioritizes qualified rural childcare projects through four existing programs for2027-2029, with licensing/health-safety requirements, geographic balancing and evaluation/reporting, without creating a universal childcare entitlement.6308 requires rural-health-liaison coordination/reporting on farm stress services.

6417 expands existing rural-hospital refinancing to the ten defined health-facility types, including rural clinics, critical-access/rural-emergency facilities, home-health agencies and community health centers. Resources, financial-hardship/stability, planning and existing preservation-of-care-access/financial-feasibility/security conditions delimit assistance. The Secretary MAY waive the named inability-to-obtain-other-credit condition for an insolvent facility, not all loan conditions. Program-specific rural/population exceptions remain; eligibility is not uniformly every facility in any place below50,000 people. Tailored technical assistance may address construction, telehealth, records, finance and grant/loan access, with priority for existing borrowers/grantees and no more than$2million annually authorized for2027-2031. These changes take effect upon completion of rulemaking.6423 extends the existing regional Delta consortium health-care/public-health-services/education authority at$3million annually for2027-2031; it is not nationwide universal coverage.

7108 extends the separate expanded food/nutrition education program's$90million annual authorization through2031 for direct low-income-family nutrition education. It does not restore SNAP-Ed's2036a grants eliminated after fiscal2025 by Public Law119-21.7204 extends existing pulse-crop health/nutrition research ($25million annually) and the Comprehensive Food Safety Training Network ($20million annually, until spent) through2031 alongside agricultural research changes; animal/crop health and exposure research are not patient-care guarantees.7209 adds education/support for youth and young adults with disabilities interested in farming and extends AgrAbility's$5million annual authority, retaining rehabilitation/referral, farmer-family and veteran safeguards.7402 extends the Farm and Ranch Stress Assistance Network's$10million annual authority, adds crisis hotlines, permits referral partnerships with specified clinical providers and requires a two-year farmer/rancher mental/tele-mental-health availability/use assessment. Service coordination and reports do not assure each person treatment.12407 extends the$3million annual emergency/transitional pet-shelter/housing grant authority through2031 for defined domestic/dating-violence, sexual-assault and stalking victims with animals. Existing24month assistance plus conditional six-month extension, confidentiality, no mandatory services/protective-order/criminal-justice-participation conditions and administrative cap remain.12410 extends already-enacted Public Law119-69 school-lunch milk/nondairy options, substitution protections, sales rules and milk-fat saturated-fat treatment to school breakfast. It permits whole milk; it does not require every child to drink it or newly create lunch authority.

TitleIII changes international food assistance as part of the wider package.3101 transfers the defined Food for Peace authorities/assets/liabilities from USAID to USDA at enactment, covering authorities held fromJanuary1,2026 onward, with State consultation.3102 narrows emergency overriding authority from any other LAW to this ACT, adds eligible NGOs and limits non-US-commodity/ocean-transport expenses to50percent of available TitleII funds.3103 repeals1724's tonnage/nonemergency and processed/fortified/bagged-commodity minima with their waivers; it does not repeal every dollar minimum.3110 retains the nonemergency$365million floor/30percent ceiling and adds$200million annually for2027-2031 from emergency TitleII funds for ready-to-use therapeutic child-wasting food ONLY when the latest specified under-five wasting estimate exceeds5percent AND annual TitleII funds exceed$1.2billion. This uses available funds, not a new unconditional appropriation.3106 requires at least$15million annually for2027-2031 from available TitleII funds for the food-relief partnership, available until spent; related consultation, quality and oversight/reporting remain.3308 extends McGovern-Dole and changes developing-country local/regional procurement from up-to10percent to8-15percent. Adding lower-middle-income countries concerns payment of internal transport/storage/handling costs under1736o-1(c)(2)(B), not general eligibility for every food-assistance activity; underlying poverty/net-food-import/education conditions remain. These programs include school food and defined child/pregnant/nursing nutrition assistance, not evidence that assistance was delivered.

The temporal baseline matters. Public Law119-37 section5002 already extends specified2018 farm authorities through the later ofSeptember30,2026 or later applicable statutory dates, subject to its exceptions and appropriation conditions. Printed2023 expiries in amended clauses do not establish that every program had already ended. Public Law119-21's prior SNAP eligibility/work-rule/cost-sharing and SNAP-Ed changes are distinct current law; this passage vote does not newly enact those earlier changes or repeal them wholesale. Floor opponents opposed the package and argued that it fails to undo earlier SNAP cuts and permits problematic contracting; floor proponents defended the provisions and urged passage. These are attributed competing arguments, not adopted fiscal/participation estimates, causal findings, motives or proof of health outcomes. Adopted Luna28 removed the three specified pesticide regulatory/liability sections before passage; the earlier general debate about those sections cannot establish that they remained in the final package. The floor opponent's inserted relief/recommittal text was an unoffered alternative; roll153 is a failed bare recommittal, not support/opposition to that printed substitute.

A Yea supported passage of this entire exact farm package, including its qualified nutrition, rural-care and social-service provisions. A Nay opposed passage of that package. Neither establishes separate positions on SNAP contracting, hot chicken, food guidelines, clinical refinancing, pesticides or any other component, or a preferred alternative. House passage is not enactment, funded awards, restored benefits, achieved food/care access or predicted fiscal/nutrition outcomes.

Immigration qualification of this same whole-passage choice is grounded in the explicit loan eligibility operators, with the other cross-border and personal-status references kept in their own scopes. The complete 959629-character governed EH was read through the attestation and footer. That reading is not an independent raw-HTML or complete Congressional Record reconstruction, a certificate of current-law integration, or editorial acceptance. All original unapproved Health meaning, source identities, claim bindings and limitations above remain part of this same core. Yea supports and Nay opposes passage of the entire package; neither establishes a separate position on any mechanism below.

Sections5101 and5201 replace each printed 'a majority' in the second sentence of7USC1922(a)(1) and1941(a)(1) with 'at least a 50 percent'. In the separately retained2024 statutory parents, that sentence applies conditions including United States citizenship to individual applicants and, for the named entity forms, individuals holding the specified interest. The proposal changes that statutory interest threshold, including the exactly50percent boundary, without deleting the citizenship words or converting every other condition into citizenship. Direct-loan experience, family-farm/operator and inability-to-obtain-credit predicates remain distinct. Section5301 likewise replaces the printed majority threshold in the first sentence of1961(a), whose individual and entity-interest clauses include citizenship, while reorganizing that subsection. This is a source-grounded reason to propose Immigration membership; it is not a conclusion that a particular noncitizen becomes eligible, that only citizens currently qualify, or that the bill supplies immigration status or work authorization.

The loan baselines have a material qualification: the separately preserved January1,2024 direct-loan regulation764.101(c) also names United States noncitizen nationals and qualified aliens for applicants and note signers. The guaranteed-loan regulation762.120(d) separately names those classes, requires the majority entity interest to be held by members in the listed classes, and requires appropriate immigration-status documentation for noncitizen nationals and qualified aliens. These are dated regulatory comparators, not a substituted text of the bill's statutory amendments or an adjudication of their interaction. Later regulations, other controlling law, exact entity structures, signature obligations and individual applications remain for legal/source review. No numerical beneficial-ownership calculation or beneficiary finding is made.

The adjacent loan operators must not be collapsed into that threshold.5101 adds qualified-operator, operating-only entity and embedded-entity rules. Its operating-only rule requires one or more real-estate owners to own at least50percent, or the other percentage the Secretary determines appropriate, of the applicant; its embedded rule retains the at-least75percent condition in its own terms.5201 changes its own operating-loan paragraph and5301 supplies separate emergency-loan rules. In the dated1961(a) parent, the fifth sentence deleted by5301 is the embedded-entity direct-ownership sentence; the bill adds replacement special rules rather than deleting citizenship or all disaster/credit predicates.12420 separately brings defined commercial fishing and fish processing into the named loan definitions and purposes, with different permitted ownership-loan and operating-loan uses and implementation steps. These provisions do not establish that every fishery participant receives a loan or that personal eligibility predicates are waived.

3306 creates a two-way agricultural cultural-immersion and exchange program. The outgoing eligible candidate must meet all four printed conditions: age19-30, demonstrated relevant experience, preparation to live in one or more host countries under the literal duration wording 'for at least 2 months or up to 6 months', whose application remains unresolved, and United States residence. Incoming placement in United States host families expressly requires the age condition and residence in an eligible country; it does not simply import all four outgoing conditions. The purpose's reference to developing United States citizens does not rewrite the eligibility word 'resident' into 'citizen'. Eligible countries have agricultural trade relations recognized by the named Service. Administration requires a qualified nonprofit cooperative agreement, the specified memorandum-of-understanding priority and equal non-Federal matching funds.10million dollars annually for2027-2031 is authorization, not proof of appropriation, placement, visa issuance, admission or work permission.7118's separate international institutional partnerships and outgoing internships/fellowships likewise do not themselves establish personal admission status.

2502(g) and8507 provide different discretionary direct-hire authorities: qualified NRCS technical-assistance candidates subject to OPM qualification standards, and qualified defined Job Corps graduates for Forest Service competitive-service positions. Both retain the printed exceptions for5USC3303 and3328 within the specified subchapter-I waiver.3303 concerns Congressional recommendations;3328 concerns Selective Service registration with its veteran exception and knowing-and-willful adjudication safeguards. The Job Corps graduate definition concerns actual voluntary selection/enrollment and educational or career-training completion; it is not a synonym for any former enrollee or a newly created immigration classification. No general citizenship, work-authorization, Selective Service or qualification waiver, actual appointment or individual registration determination is inferred.

7608 requires the specified interagency research activities to be applied consistently with CHIPS divisionB/titleVI/subtitleD. The provisions in the dated19231-19237 comparator distinguish research-agency personnel from covered award individuals, require the stated disclosures/certifications/training, retain proof, privacy and rebuttal/appeal safeguards, preserve qualified open international collaboration and foreign-student advising, and prohibit targeting or discrimination based on race, ethnicity or national origin. They are not a blanket prohibition on foreign students or foreign-born researchers.7614 separately concerns vertebrate-animal research, education or extension in or with China, Russia or defined countries of concern, with its sole-official, necessity and30day-notice waiver; it does not bar all international science or all people from those countries. No actual agency policy, listing, misconduct or nationality determination is made.

9012's solar-component funding exclusion and10006's microorganism pilot use different actors and predicates. The former concerns specified components made in a defined country of concern or by the named domiciled/controlled entity or defined foreign entity of concern. The latter requires an eligible responsible legal entity with a United States physical address, no specified government ownership/affiliation and every other printed experience, facility, containment and compliance predicate. Its75party interstate-microorganism pilot, inspection, release-reporting, disenrollment and appeal provisions govern plant pests, not the admission or removal of people. The CHIPS country and entity definitions retain all their own listed/designated, ownership/control, allegation-plus-conviction and determination branches. No automatic finding that a foreign company, individual or laboratory satisfies them is made.

12301-12305 revise AFIDA information sharing, reporting/enforcement, database and agricultural-transaction review. The original3501 reporting obligations and3508 individual, entity, government, land and State definitions are separately preserved. The individual citizenship/nationality/permanent-residence/parole words and literal disjunctions are not silently changed to a conjunction or converted into a universal present-law classification. The January1,2024 regulation781.2 separately retains its agricultural-land, interest exclusions and significant-interest/control definitions; it does not certify the future enactment-date regulation incorporated by12304.12301 distinguishes nonreporting's maximum25percent penalty from knowingly incomplete/misleading/false reporting's5-25percent range; public identification concerns persons who paid a penalty, with an appeal completed where applicable, not a finding that every foreign owner violated the law. The rulemaking, investigation, outreach and database provisions do not establish actual misconduct or ownership.

12302's covered foreign person requires both the incorporated AFIDA foreign-person definition and citizenship in, or headquarters in, a covered country as applicable. A title about state sponsors does not replace that operative definition.12303's newly incorporated foreign-entity-of-concern definition is15USC4651, distinct from42USC19237; its natural-person protected-individual exclusion and other entity/control/agency branches remain separate. The printed phrases about citizenship/headquarters in a foreign entity of concern and the government of such an entity are retained as printed, with their legal application unresolved.12304 defines 'database' by reference to(c) while development is in(b); no repair is supplied. It withholds the name and price from public disclosure for at least30days; this is not automatic unrestricted publication on day31.

12305 makes Agriculture a CFIUS member for the specified covered agricultural transactions. Its reportable-land transaction has all three printed predicates, including reason to believe based on intelligence information/cooperation, acquisition by the listed four-country foreign person and an AFIDA reporting requirement. CFIUS must determine coverage and, only if covered, whether to initiate review or take another authorized action; not every transaction automatically receives a full review. Its sunset is country-specific removal from the referenced regulatory list.12306 separately directs presidentially ordered regulations prohibiting land purchase by defined foreign adversaries, state sponsors, their agents/instrumentalities and owned/controlled/affiliated persons. Its foreign-adversary definition is conduct-based, not every noncitizen. Neither clause is a new visa, admission or removal ground. The differing printed50USC4318/4813 citations and entity/country words are not normalized; integration, actual lists and individual ownership/legal consequences remain unresolved.

The incorporated 11 U.S.C.101(6) and103(d) connect that treatment to commodity-broker liquidation in chapter7; section109(d) excludes commodity brokers from ordinary chapter11 eligibility. Under section766(h), the customer-property pool is distributed ratably to customers up to their allowed net-equity claims before other claims, except the specified section507(a)(2) administrative claims attributable to administering that property. Proprietary-account customer claims wait until other customer net-equity claims have been paid in full. The other creditor claims include qualifying allowed unsecured employee-benefit contribution claims under section507(a)(5); the accompanying legislative notes expressly identify health-insurance plans within that category.
